question: According to Karri Saarinen, why does good design become more important as product categories grow crowded?
expected_points: Design can help a product stand out among many alternatives.

evidence_quote: When people have a lot of choices, they probably will pick the one that looks most interesting.

sections.heading: Design helps people choose in a crowded category
sections.content: When people have many choices, they may not know which specific feature they want, so they compare products and look for the one that seems highest-quality or most interesting. Because people are visual, strong product design can make a product stand out and draw them to it. Brand design can also pull people toward a company: Saarinen uses Nike as an example of people choosing a familiar brand even when another shoe might be better.

sections.heading: The bar rises as categories mature
sections.content: Saarinen says the first products in a new paradigm do not necessarily need to be highly polished, but later entrants face a much higher bar. He contrasts early, basic websites from companies such as Google and YouTube with what would get attention today, and says products need high-level design from the beginning to be taken seriously. He also cautions that design is not by itself the reason a company succeeds: the product still needs to be better or different in some way.

sections.heading: Design can improve perception and acquisition
sections.content: Good design or brand can draw people in and improve user acquisition, retention, and perception. Saarinen compares this to packaging that sets expectations of quality before someone uses a product, and says a startup’s landing page can do similar work, especially early on when few people know the company.

sections.heading: Why design matters more in crowded categories
sections.content: With many choices, people may not know exactly which feature they want, so they compare products and use visual impressions to judge quality. A product that looks best or most interesting can stand out and draw users. As categories mature and competitors multiply, the baseline rises: early products in a new paradigm can be basic, but a crowded field—Karri’s example is email clients—requires good design just to be considered seriously. He also notes that design and brand can improve perception and help attract or retain users.

sections.heading: Caveat

answer.summary: As categories fill with alternatives, customers often cannot identify a must-have feature, so they compare products and gravitate toward the one that looks most interesting or highest quality. Meanwhile, the design bar rises: products need strong design just to be taken seriously. Product and brand design can therefore help a company stand out and attract users.

sections.heading: More choices make design a signal of quality
sections.content: When a category offers many choices, people may not know which specific feature they want. They compare products visually, and design can make one seem like the best or highest-quality option—so it stands out and is more likely to be chosen. Brand design can also draw people to a product, as Saarinen illustrates with Nike: people may choose the familiar brand even if another shoe could be better.

sections.heading: The baseline rises as categories mature
sections.content: Saarinen says early products in a new paradigm—such as the web or mobile—did not necessarily need to be highly designed because they were first. As a category fills with alternatives, the bar rises: an email client has to be pretty good to be considered one, and a basic website that might have worked for an early entrant may no longer get attention. Strong design becomes important just to be taken seriously.
